draft.title: Surface area of a cylinder
card: A closed cylinder has three surfaces: a circle for the top, a circle for the base and a curved surface around the side.
The curved surface unrolls into a rectangle. Its length is the circle's circumference, \(2\pi r\), and its width is the height \(h\). Its area is \(2\pi r h\).
two circles plus the curved surface, so \(A = 2\pi r^{2} + 2\pi r h\).
one circle plus the curved surface, so \(A = \pi r^{2} + 2\pi r h\). Example: a closed cylinder with \(r = 3\) and \(h = 10\) has \(A = 18\pi + 60\pi = 78\pi \approx 245.0\) \(\text{cm}^{2}\).
draft.remember: Add the circles you have to the curved rectangle of area \(2\pi r h\).

a.q: What is the area of the curved surface of a cylinder with radius 4 cm and height 9 cm?
a.why: The curved surface is a rectangle of length \(2\pi \times 4 = 8\pi\) and width 9, so its area is \(72\pi \text{ cm}^{2}\). \(32\pi \text{ cm}^{2}\) is the area of the two circles, not the curved surface.
a.clue: Unroll the side into a rectangle and find its length and width.

b.q: A metal bucket in Wagga has no lid. It is a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 20 cm. What is the area of metal used, to the nearest \(\text{cm}^{2}\)?
b.why: The bucket is open, so it has one circle: \(\pi \times 7^{2} = 49\pi\). The curved surface is \(2\pi \times 7 \times 20 = 280\pi\). The total is \(329\pi \approx 1034\) \(\text{cm}^{2}\). Using two circles gives \(1188 \text{ cm}^{2}\), which is for a closed cylinder.
b.clue: Count how many circles the bucket has.
